raw_plan.interpretation: One acquisition email for the selected solution-aware audience, narrowed per the current dossier to freelancers delivering a client project. The email introduces the Your Plans on Paper planner as a bounded, self-serve 16-week planning option and sends the reader to the documented personalisation-and-basket action.

intent.reason_now: A freelancer beginning a client project may be evaluating how to structure a focused work cycle; no deadline, launch event or recipient history is assumed.
intent.desired_action: Personalise the Your Plans on Paper planner and add it to the basket.

raw_plan.reader: A freelancer evaluating a paper-based structure for a focused client project that could fit a 16-week planning cycle.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A goal-driven professional starting a focused 16-week push and wanting planning away from screens
raw_plan.reader_scope: Freelancers delivering a client project; do not generalise the proposition to every goal-driven professional or every kind of project.
raw_plan.promise: Papier gives a freelancer a bounded, undated 16-week paper structure for mapping a client project across monthly, weekly and daily planning horizons.
raw_plan.orientation: For a freelancer delivering a client project, Papier offers an undated paper productivity planner for a focused 16-week cycle.
raw_plan.arc: In this single-email campaign, move the reader from knowing only that Papier sells planners to being able to judge whether this planner's specific 16-week, undated structure suits a client project and, if so, personalise it.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: One email must complete the acquisition argument by itself. Lead with the most relevant, checkable mechanism—the 16-week span and undated monthly, weekly and daily pages—then invite the reader to assess that fit at the product destination. Do not manufacture a failed workflow or claim that the planner is simple to maintain. No alternative proposition is included because tracking tools and reflections are less concrete for this first buying decision and their exact formats are undocumented.

emails.selection_reason: A defined 16-week planning span directly matches the audience's bounded-project context, while the undated monthly, weekly and daily pages give the reader concrete criteria they can assess without relying on testimonials or promised outcomes.
emails.target_audience: Freelancers delivering a client project within the selected audience of goal-driven professionals seeking planning away from screens.
emails.job: Earn a product evaluation by helping the reader decide whether an undated 16-week paper planner fits the shape of an upcoming client project.
emails.single_idea: If a client project suits a focused 16-week push, Your Plans on Paper provides a finite, undated structure with monthly, weekly and daily planning pages rather than an open-ended planning commitment.
emails.mechanism: The planner contains 16 weeks of planning on undated pages and provides monthly, weekly and daily planning views, allowing the reader to inspect one bounded paper structure for the project.
emails.belief_shift: Before: the reader does not know how this Papier planner maps to a bounded client project. After: the reader can judge it as a specific 16-week, undated structure spanning monthly, weekly and daily planning.
must_not_say: Do not claim the planner is uncomplicated, effortless or proven to be maintainable.
Do not claim it guarantees focus, productivity, accountability, timely delivery or a successful client outcome.
Do not state or imply that the recipient currently uses, dislikes or has failed with any particular app, calendar or planning system.
Do not claim the planner replaces digital calendars, reminders or project-management tools, or that it integrates with them.
Do not cite customer adoption, testimonials, measured results or social proof.
Do not claim uniqueness, superiority or an exclusive advantage over competing planners.
Do not broaden the established fit from freelancers delivering a client project to all professionals or all projects.
Do not introduce price, dividers, shipping, sustainability, returns or the satisfaction policy; they do not carry this email's argument.
emails.objection: Will this planner's scope and layout fit the project well enough to justify personalising it? Answer with the documented 16-week span and planning views, not with an unsupported claim that it is easy to maintain.
emails.tone: Encouraging, focused and practical, with a light sense of possibility rather than urgency.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether this 16-week, undated monthly-to-daily planning structure is a suitable paper framework for the client project.
emails.next_step_value: The destination lets the reader proceed with the Your Plans on Paper planner after assessing its documented 16-week span and monthly, weekly and daily planning structure.
emails.next_step_limit: This step does not establish that the planner will be easy to maintain, replace digital tools, improve project delivery or produce any particular professional result.
emails.subject_strategy: Make the concrete 16-week project horizon the reason to open, with a subtle paper-planning cue; avoid generic productivity language, urgency and promised outcomes.

raw_plan.voice_notes: Use Papier's imaginative but specific register: make putting plans on paper feel inviting, while keeping the 16-week structure central. Avoid productivity clichés and do not imply that screens or digital tools are inherently ineffective.

events.subject: Put a 16-week project on paper
events.preview_text: See how one undated planner moves from monthly milestones to daily work.
events.body:
Map a client project across 16 weeks on paper. Papier’s Your Plans on Paper is an undated productivity planner for shaping that finite stretch of work.

Monthly pages hold the wider project horizon. Weekly and daily pages give you space to bring the next pieces into view, all within the same 16-week structure.

That bounded span makes the fit easier to judge: does the project call for one focused planning cycle, with room to move between its milestones and the work of each day?

The link opens the personalisation page, where you can personalise the planner and add it to your basket.

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Map 16 weeks on paper"
events.subject: Map 16 weeks on paper
events.preview_text: See how undated monthly, weekly and daily planning could frame a client project.
events.body:
For a client project with a defined horizon, plans can be mapped at three levels: the month ahead, the coming week and today. Papier’s Your Plans on Paper is a softback spiral productivity planner that brings those views together across **16 weeks**.

Its monthly, weekly and daily planning pages are undated. That gives you one bounded paper structure to assess against the shape of a focused client project, without tying the plan to fixed calendar dates.

If that scope fits the project, the link opens the Your Plans on Paper personalisation page, where you can personalise the planner and add it to your basket.

Papier’s Your Plans on Paper is an undated productivity planner with **16 weeks** of planning. For a focused client project, that puts a defined stretch of work on paper, with pages that aren’t tied to fixed calendar dates.

Its monthly, weekly and daily planning pages let you consider the same project at three horizons: across the 16-week span, the week ahead and what belongs on today’s page. The question is simply whether those views fit the way you want to plan.

If they do, the link opens the Your Plans on Paper personalisation page. You can personalise the planner there and add it to your basket.
